_comment: The gateway mapping that gives D2 `outcome-materialise` a URL the PUBLISHER can POST a
decision to. This is the return path under the decided design (plan section 8.7): no
export, no import, no capture stream, no republish -- the publisher makes an ordinary
HTTPS call to the DISTRIBUTOR's own gateway, and cerberus stamps x-account-id from that
gateway's config (gateway_api.go:2111). Tenancy is therefore the distributor's with zero
platform work, which is the whole reason this path was chosen over the granted four hops.
On the pilot account this mapping is on antipodean_build's own gateway (VWqPwSvI9DMS)
because no second staging account was available -- see the delivery report. In a real
distribution this file is installed on the DISTRIBUTOR's gateway and the gateway_id, url
and resource all change; the shape does not.
Three calls, in order, then a fourth to force a route-table rebuild:

mapping_version.description: D2 outcome-materialise: the publisher projects a decision here

traps: Step 3 is not optional. POST /mapping never sets traffic_distribution and cerberus skips every version whose weight is 0, so the route mounts with an empty version list and dies in the recoverer as a 500 with an EMPTY BODY.

The route table can be stale for minutes. `bcli publish ms.gateway.<id>.reload` cannot reach a sub-account; PATCH /gateway/<id> with a description writes ms.gateway.<id>.gateway, which cerberus turns into a per-gateway rebuild. Doing it in the same script as the three calls meant the route served on the first request.

An ERRORED flow run returns the whole node list to the HTTP caller -- node ids, urls, eval source and static references. Header VALUES are redacted ([redacted], P17), so no credential escapes, but on a distributor-facing endpoint the publisher's flow internals do. Nothing distributor-facing should be allowed to error; return a status field instead.
invocation_type must be RequestResponse or the gateway does not await the run and the caller gets nothing to read.
